title: Fitness components
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:51Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the full list of nine fitness components in the brief: the health-related fitness point covers only four of them (aerobic power, strength, endurance, flexibility) and the fitness testing point teaches how to test fitness, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Fitness components
card: Aerobic power
the highest rate at which the body can use oxygen to make energy. It supports long efforts.
Anaerobic capacity
the total energy the body can make without oxygen. It supports hard efforts lasting seconds to a couple of minutes.
Strength, power, endurance
Muscular strength is the most force a muscle can produce. Power is force applied quickly. Muscular endurance is repeating contractions without tiring.
Speed, agility, flexibility, body composition
Speed is how fast the body moves. Agility is changing direction quickly. Flexibility is the range of movement at a joint. Body composition is the share of fat, muscle and bone.
draft.remember: Each fitness component is a different physical quality, and activities need them in different amounts.

a.q: Which fitness component is the ability to change direction quickly?
a.why: Agility is changing direction quickly. Speed is tempting, but it is how fast the body moves, not how well it changes direction.
a.clue: Think of a netball player dodging a defender.

b.q: Tom, a rower, rows 2000 m at a steady pace for 7 minutes, using oxygen to supply most of his energy. Which component is the best match for the quality he needs most?
b.why: A long effort fuelled by oxygen depends on aerobic power. Muscular strength is tempting because rowing uses force, but strength is the most force in a single effort, not the oxygen use that supports a long effort.
b.clue: Which component is about using oxygen for long efforts?

problems.detail: The stem says Tom is 'using oxygen to supply most of his energy', which repeats the card's definition of aerobic power. The clue restates it again. A student can match the words without understanding the idea, and two of the distractors (flexibility, agility) are plainly unrelated.

Muscular endurance is defined as 'repeating contractions without tiring'. Muscles do tire. The quality is the ability to sustain repeated contractions over time while resisting fatigue, so 'without tiring' could mislead.

check.summary: The answers are correct and the card's facts are sound. Question b gives its answer away by naming oxygen use in the stem, and the card's 'without tiring' for muscular endurance is slightly inaccurate.

a.why: Agility is changing direction quickly. Speed is tempting, but it is how fast the body moves, not how well it changes direction.

b.q: Priya runs 400 m in about 55 seconds. She reaches top speed early but slows sharply over the last 100 m. Which component would most help her hold her pace?
b.why: A flat-out effort of under a minute draws mainly on energy made without oxygen, and slowing late shows that supply is running low. Speed is tempting, but Priya already reaches top speed. Her problem is keeping it, and aerobic power suits much longer efforts.
b.clue: How long and how hard is her race?
